description: Pull canceled subscriptions directly from a Postgres or MySQL database and analyze them for churn patterns. Requires POSTGRES_URL or MYSQL_URL env var (use a read-only database user ,  see retentioncheck.com/integrations for the exact SQL to create one). You describe your schema in plain arguments (table, cancelled_at_column, reason_column, etc.) and the tool generates a safe parameterized SELECT query. Includes plan MRR, sub age, and schema-mismatch detection with actionable errors. Defaults to last 90 days.

dialect.description: Which SQL dialect. Reads POSTGRES_URL or MYSQL_URL from env accordingly.

focus.description: Optional focus area to narrow the analysis (e.g., 'pricing', 'onboarding').

lookback_days.description: How many days back to analyze. Defaults to 90. Min 7. Max 365.

schema.description: Schema mapping that tells the tool which columns hold what.

cancelled_at_column.description: Column name storing the cancellation timestamp. Used to filter by lookback_days.

customer_tenure_days_column.description: Column storing the sub age in days at time of cancellation. Used for 'age Nd' context in feedback lines.

mrr_column.description: Column storing monthly revenue for the canceled subscription (used for MRR impact estimates).

mrr_unit.description: Unit for mrr_column. Defaults to 'dollars'. Use 'cents' if you store Stripe-style integer cents.

reason_column.description: Column storing the cancellation reason (enum or free text). Optional but recommended.

status_filter.description: Optional filter on a status column. Useful if canceled rows sit in the same table as active rows.

table.description: Table name containing subscription/cancellation records. Only letters, digits, underscores allowed.

name: analyze_sql_churn
title: Analyze Churn from SQL Database
